finding: KS cum_bad is built as flag(pl.col('default_flag') != 0).cum_sum(), an independent second comparison, instead of the ELSE branch of the SAS if/else. SAS :96-97 adds 1 to cum_bad for every row that is not default_flag = 0, including a missing default_flag (missing = 0 is false, so the row takes the else branch). In the port, null != 0 is null and flag() turns it into 0. Probe (scratch latent.py): default_flag [0, ., 1, 0] gives port cum_bad [0,0,1,1] where SAS gives [0,1,2,2]. That shifts cum_pct_bad, ks_value and possibly KS_Statistic/KS_Cutoff. The four judged inputs have no missing default_flag, and all of them reproduce ks_statistic.csv byte-for-byte, so the effect is latent. But the code contradicts the inventory text it cites.
cites: RULEBOOK §2 'if A then ...; else ...' row (one when/otherwise chain preserving first-match semantics); inventory.tsv row 107 metrics_calculation.sas work.ks_calculation / ks_statistic ('cum_bad = cumulative count of everything else (:96-97, else branch)'); metrics_calculation.sas:96-97
fix: Derive cum_bad from the same condition as cum_good: cum_bad=(1 - sas_compat.flag(pl.col('default_flag') == 0)).cum_sum(), or pl.when(pl.col('default_flag') == 0).then(0).otherwise(1).cum_sum().

finding: The calibration_plot aggregation uses bare polars pl.col('pd_logistic').sum() and pl.col('default_flag').sum() (:288-289) to translate SQL mean(). v1.3 S10 forbids bare .sum() for PROC SQL aggregates, because it returns 0 where SAS returns missing. The same file uses sas_compat.sql_sum for the identical decile pd_sum (:167), so the file is also inconsistent. The divergence is concrete: rows with a missing pd_logistic all land in the pred_bin = . group. There the port prints mean_predicted 0 and mean_actual 0 (probe: null bin -> 0.0, 0.0), while SAS mean() over all-missing values is missing (empty field). This is latent on the judged inputs (pd never missing; all four calibration_plot.csv files are byte-identical). Inventory rows 136-138 still spell out the bare .sum(): they predate S10, and the rulebook wins.
cites: RULEBOOK §2 'PROC SQL aggregates sum/mean/min/max(x)' row (S10: sas_compat.sql_sum/sql_mean ... never bare polars .sum()); inventory.tsv rows 136-138 metrics_calculation.sas calibration_plot.csv / work.calibration_plot (stale wording); metrics_calculation.sas:310-311
fix: _sum_pd=sas_compat.sql_sum(pl.col('pd_logistic')), _defaults=sas_compat.sql_sum(pl.col('default_flag')), the same as decile_analysis :166-167. Queue an inventory correction for rows 136-138.

finding: The SQL remerge filter uses a plain pl.col('ks_value') == max. In PROC SQL, missing = missing is TRUE. If ks_value is missing on every row (an input with no defaults or no non-defaults, so total_*_count = 0 and cum_* / 0 is missing), SAS max() is missing. The WHERE then keeps EVERY row: KS_Statistic missing and KS_Cutoff = each pd. The port's == null keeps none, so ks_statistic.csv is header-only and the merges are 1 row instead of N. The comparison at :110 has no MISSING_NEVER/NULLABLE classification in inventory row 107 (its sites S222-S239 carry only ORDER;PROC_SEMANTICS). The implementer used the plain form without proving never-missing and without flagging the gap. This is unreachable on the four judged inputs: both classes are present, KS is reproduced exactly, and roc_association would also fail first.
cites: RULEBOOK §2 comparison row + A2 (plain form only where the row proves MISSING_NEVER); RULEBOOK §5 (site not classified -> flag it, UNKNOWN rule); inventory.tsv row 107; metrics_calculation.sas:105-110
fix: Either use sas_compat.eq(pl.col('ks_value'), max) (SQL: missing = missing true; eq is 'no site; unverified' per A31), or keep == and add '# TODO(port): ks_value can be missing when one class is absent; inventory row 107 has no MISSING classification' (and bump todos=1). Queue an inventory row.
